A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlashRNN and ConstrINT work. All 23 pages in each version, including equations, figures, tables and Appendices A-K, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original kernel runtime measurements, SlimPajama language-model training results, parity-task accuracies, and appendix roofline and numerical-error analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendices G-I, including runtime plots and Tables 1-3.

M1.justification: The fused and alternating kernels, Triton implementation, head-wise parallelization, gradient clipping and ConstrINT procedure are unchanged. The equation edits do not establish a changed implementation; Algorithms 1-5 remain the same.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same SlimPajama language-modeling task, synthetic parity extrapolation task and LSTM/sLSTM kernel benchmarks. No dataset, task or hardware test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding runtime comparisons retain FlashAttention2, PyTorch nn.LSTM/cuDNN and Haste. Language-model and parity comparator sets also match, as do the torch.compile and float64 comparisons in Appendix H.

E3.justification: Model sizes, precision, hardware, batch/head/sequence sweeps and training budgets are unchanged. Both retain language-model training on 15B tokens and parity training up to length 40 with evaluation at lengths 40-256; Appendices J-K report identical settings.

E4.justification: The roofline analysis, fused-kernel size limits, runtime scaling experiments, external gate-preactivation comparison and numerical-error analysis are retained unchanged in Appendices G-H. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both report runtime averages over 1000 measured iterations and parity accuracies averaged over three seeds at the selected learning rate. No repeated-run information, uncertainty reporting or statistical testing practice changes.

E6.justification: Tables 1-3 and the empirical plots retain their results. For example, Table 2 reports Transformer/Mamba/mLSTM accuracies of 0.52/0.56/0.54 and 1.00 for Elman, GRU, LSTM and sLSTM in both versions.

T1.justification: Equation (4) replaces the unsummed recurrent-gradient contribution with an explicit sum over gates. Equations (2)-(4) also specify state/gate index ranges, although the new one-based ranges conflict with Appendix A's zero-based labels. The remaining derivations and complexity analysis are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims, including up to 50x speedups, 40x larger hidden sizes than the Triton implementation, head-wise processing and ConstrINT tuning. The revised title emphasizes an existing I/O-aware approach.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 changes parity from a litmus test for state tracking generally to a test for the 'simplest subclass' of state-tracking capabilities. This modestly narrows the interpretation of unchanged evidence; other explanations and limitations remain the same.

D1.justification: Implementation details in Appendices B-E, software and hardware specifications, training hyperparameters in Appendices J-K, and the stated source-code access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to FlashAttention, Haste and earlier RNN research are unchanged. Bibliography alphabetization, expanded author lists and corrected Gers author metadata concern the same references.

P1.justification: The title changes to 'I/O-Aware Optimization of Traditional RNNs on modern hardware.' Citation formatting, bibliography order, acknowledgments and a related-work paragraph break are revised. The main narrative and section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 corrects recurrent-product labels from R h_t to R h_{t-1}. Expanded equations and reformatted references cause limited layout changes; the remaining figures and table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves precision through the narrower parity-test interpretation, corrected Figure 1 labels and explicit gate aggregation in Equation (4). The mathematical cleanup is incomplete because its new index ranges conflict with Appendix A. These limited clarity gains improve the paper slightly, while its methods and empirical support remain unchanged.
